title: FetchJsonOutput
description:
Top-level envelope for `rwv fetch --json` (serial / `-j 1` mode).

Shape: `{ "$schema": "<url>", "outcomes": [<FetchOutcomeOutput>, ...] }`.

placements.description: How the files of each checkout the fetch moved or created were placed: a canonical clone it realigned, and from a workweave each worktree it created there. Empty, not absent, when it placed none.

resolution.description: Resolved workspace coordinates (weave root, optional workweave identity, project). Absent when no project is resolved.

skipped.description: The materialization side effects this fetch skipped, each naming the command that performs it. Empty, not absent, when it skipped none.

Effect.description: The side effect that did not happen.

oneOf.description: The integrations' install hooks (`npm install`, `uv sync`, `cargo fetch`, …).
Regenerating the integrations' managed and generated files.
Refreshing the weave root's links onto the project's files.
Activating a fetched project: selecting it, surfacing its links and running its install hooks.

FetchOutcomeOutput.description:
Per-repo outcome record for `rwv fetch --json`.

`status` is one of `"ok"`, `"skipped"`, or `"failed"`. `message` carries a human-readable description of the outcome (always present for `"failed"`; present for `"skipped"` to say why; `null` for `"ok"`).

FilePlacement.description: How a member's tracked files reached a workspace.

hardlinked.description: Linked to another workspace's read-only copy.

reflinked.description: Cloned from another workspace's copy, sharing its storage until either is written.

written.description: Written by the version control system.

PlacementOutput.description: How the files of one checkout were placed when a verb created or moved it.

absolute_path.description: The checkout whose files were placed.

files.description: How many files were cloned, linked or written.

Resolution.description:
Resolved workspace coordinates for `--json` output and the plugin env-var envelope.

Carries `workspace` (primary root abs path), `workweave` (the `<project>--<name>` identity the registry records), `project` (resolved project name), and `workweave_unregistered`. No `kind` or `location` field: the checkout is one of three states, and two of them are already carried by `workweave`'s presence.

The third state needs a field of its own. A workweave whose directory no registry entry names has no identity, so `workweave` is absent for it — and absent is what the primary looks like. Without `workweave_unregistered` the two serialize identically, and a consumer reading the documented meaning of that absence is told, positively, that it is at the primary checkout.

Results only — provenance (which chain step resolved the project, which flag addressed the workspace) is deliberately excluded: anything in default `--json` output becomes depended on, and the assertion use case needs the result, not the mechanism. Provenance appears only in the human-facing "target:" line printed to stderr.

Isomorphic to the plugin env-var envelope (`RWV_WORKSPACE`/`RWV_WORKWEAVE`/`RWV_WORKWEAVE_UNREGISTERED`/`RWV_PROJECT`): both surfaces are pure projections of [`WorkspaceContext::resolution`], never independently computed.

workspace.description:
Primary weave root, in the wire spelling.

A `String` and not a `PathBuf` so the spelling is decided at construction rather than by serde: this is a published absolute path and it owes programs the composable form, which [`crate::path_spelling::wire_path`] is the only producer of.

workweave.description:
Workweave identity (`<project>--<name>`), as the primary-side registry records it.

Absent at the primary, and absent for a workweave whose directory no registry entry names — identity is by record, so an unregistered workweave has no identity to report and rwv will not spell one from the directory name. Those two absences are told apart by `workweave_unregistered`, not by this field.

workweave_unregistered.description:
`true` when the invocation resolved into a workweave whose directory no registry entry names, so `workweave` above is absent for a reason that is not "this is the primary".

Serialized only in that state, so the primary and a registered workweave emit exactly the bytes they emitted before this field existed. `rwv doctor --fix` registers such a directory, after which this is absent and `workweave` carries the identity.

SkipReason.description: Why the effect did not happen.

oneOf.description: An authoring verb ran inside a workweave, where it runs no hooks.
The CLI the integration's hook drives is not on `PATH`.
The verb acted on a project the weave root does not present.
A project was already active, so the fetch selected none.

SkippedEffect.description: One materialization side effect a verb skipped on this run.

integration.description: The integration whose part of `effect` was skipped; absent when the whole effect was.

remedy.description: The command that performs the effect.
